newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia parliament to re-examine broadcast bill.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia parliament to re-examine broadcast bill.

text.p: Indonesia's parliament intends to re-examine a broadcasting bill passed by the house last year but yet to be signed into law by President Suharto, the official Antara news agency said on Saturday.

The heads of the Golkar and United Development Party (PPP) factions in the House of Representatives supported an unreported statement by speaker Wahono to rediscuss substantive matters of the broadcasting bill passed in early December.
However, the report did not say what would be rediscussed by the mostly rubber stamp parliament or why.

"Golkar is open to discussing again the broadcasting bill in order that it can be finished. Of course, those discussions will be limited to the substance which is crucial," Golkar faction leader Moestahid Astari was quoted as saying.
"Indeed it is unusual, but we have an accommodative attitude towards the aspirations of the community," PPP faction leader Hamzah Haz said.

The broadcasting bill was the nation's first law of its type and it was aimed at protecting the domestic broadcasting industry as well as extending the law to cable television and other new multi-media technologies.

The bill had originally been submitted to parliament in March 1996 and was supposed to have become law by October that year. It was considered controversial as it would allow the state-owned TVRI television network to carry advertising.
It was passed by the house in December but Suharto has yet to sign it into law.
Following the general election in May, a new parliament is due to take up its seats in October.

Golkar party chief and former Information Minister Harmoko, now a minister for special affairs of state, is widely expected to take up the post of parliamentary speaker after he surrended his post at the information ministry to a retired general last month.
